OK.name: Oklahoma
OK.remedy: Expungement (sealing of records); Clean Slate automatic expungement for some records

misdemeanor.note: A misdemeanor conviction can be expunged 5 years after conviction if you have no felony record, no pending charges and court costs are paid (no wait if you only got a fine under $501). Under Oklahoma's Clean Slate law (HB 3316, effective Nov. 1, 2022; automatic processing began 2025) eligible misdemeanor records are expunged automatically unless a prosecutor or agency objects.
misdemeanor.issue: Old note did not mention Clean Slate automatic expungement or the no-wait rule for fine-only cases.

felony.note: One nonviolent felony can be expunged by petition 5 years after the sentence is completed if you have no other felony and no misdemeanor in the past 7 years; up to two felonies (not violent, not sex-offender registrable) after 10 years.
felony.issue: Wait runs from completion of sentence, not conviction; the 10-year two-felony route was missing.

dui.note: A misdemeanor DUI is treated like other misdemeanor convictions: it can be expunged 5 years after conviction if you have no felony and no pending charges. A felony DUI must meet the felony rules.
dui.issue: App said DUI is not eligible; § 18 has no DUI exclusion for misdemeanor convictions (CCRC lists no DUI exclusion).

dismissed.note: Acquittals, reversed convictions and uncharged arrests can be expunged, and dismissed charges qualify once you have no felony conviction and the charge cannot be refiled; dismissals after a deferred sentence wait 1 year (misdemeanor) or 10 years (felony). Many of these records are now expunged automatically under Clean Slate.
dismissed.issue: Old note omitted the Clean Slate automatic process and the deferred-sentence waiting periods.

domestic.note: A misdemeanor domestic assault conviction falls under the general misdemeanor rule (5 years after conviction). Felony domestic violence counts as a violent offense and is excluded from the nonviolent-felony routes.
domestic.issue: App said domestic offenses are barred; § 18 has no domestic-violence exclusion for misdemeanor convictions.

sexual.note: Convictions that require sex-offender registration are excluded from Oklahoma's felony and deferred-felony expungement routes. A conviction that has been pardoned may be expunged.
sexual.issue: App said fully barred; registrable offenses are excluded from felony routes but the pardon route remains.

juvenile.notes: Juvenile records are confidential; a court may seal them 1 year after the case ends, and a person 18 or older who finished all requirements and has no adult arrests may apply (orally while the case is open) for expungement. No automatic expungement.
juvenile.issue: Age was lowered from 21 to 18 in 2021 (HB 1799); no first-offense or nonviolent requirement in statute.

misdemeanor.waitFrom: conviction or release from jail, whichever is later
misdemeanor.note: A Class A misdemeanor can be set aside 3 years after conviction or release; Class B and C misdemeanors after 1 year. You must finish your sentence and have no new conviction during the wait; you file a motion with the court.

felony.waitFrom: conviction or release from prison, whichever is later
felony.note: A Class C felony can be set aside after 5 years; a Class B felony after 7 years unless it is a crime against a person. Class A felonies cannot be set aside.
felony.issue: Added that Class B non-person felonies qualify after 7 years and Class A felonies are not eligible.

dui.note: DUII convictions cannot be set aside in Oregon because traffic offenses are excluded; this applies even when a DUII diversion ended in dismissal.

dismissed.note: Acquittals and dismissed charges can be set aside at any time; an arrest or citation with no charges filed can be set aside 60 days after the prosecutor declines. You file a motion; Oregon does not seal these automatically for adults.
dismissed.issue: No adult automatic set-aside was confirmed; the Oregon Judicial Department self-help page says a motion is required.

domestic.waitFrom: conviction or release, whichever is later
domestic.note: Domestic violence convictions are not excluded as a group: a misdemeanor such as Assault IV can be set aside after 3 years. Some child- and elder-abuse offenses are excluded, and victims receive notice of the motion.
domestic.issue: App said domestic violence offenses are not eligible; ORS 137.225 has no general domestic-violence exclusion.

sexual.note: Sex crimes cannot be set aside unless they fall within narrow statutory exceptions (for example, certain lower-level offenses where the person has been relieved of registration).
sexual.issue: App said fully barred; the statute bars sex crimes 'unless' listed exceptions apply.

juvenile.when: Juvenile dept files for violation/misdemeanor-level cases; others by application after 4 years
juvenile.notes: Since SB 519 (2023, effective Jan. 1, 2024) county juvenile departments apply for expunction for youth whose cases involved conduct that would be a violation or misdemeanor for an adult (with exceptions); others may apply after a 4-year wait (cut from 5). Contacts that never led to juvenile court jurisdiction are expunged automatically.
juvenile.citation: ORS 419A.260-419A.262 (as amended by Or. Laws 2023, ch. 182 (SB 519))
juvenile.issue: App described broad automatic expunction at 18 with only Measure 11 excluded; automatic process is limited to violation/misdemeanor-level cases and the age-18 trigger was not confirmed.

PA.name: Pennsylvania
PA.remedy: Limited access (sealing), automatic under Clean Slate; expungement for non-convictions, summary offenses and age 70+

misdemeanor.note: Second- and third-degree and ungraded misdemeanors are sealed automatically after 7 years with no new felony or misdemeanor conviction, if restitution is paid (Clean Slate 3.0, Act 36 of 2023, effective Feb. 12, 2024; auto-sealing began June 11, 2024). You can also petition for sealing after 7 years.
misdemeanor.issue: App said 10-year wait and 'conditional'; Act 36 of 2023 cut the wait to 7 years and sealing is automatic.

felony.note: Lower-level drug felonies are sealed automatically after 10 conviction-free years; third-degree or ungraded felonies for theft, forgery/fraud, criminal mischief, trespass and welfare fraud can be sealed by petition after 10 years.
felony.issue: App said felonies are not eligible; Act 36 of 2023 made certain felonies eligible for sealing.

dui.note: A DUI that is a misdemeanor (a first-offense DUI is an ungraded misdemeanor) is not excluded and can be sealed automatically after 7 conviction-free years. A DUI resolved through ARD can be expunged.
dui.issue: App said DUI is not eligible; Clean Slate Initiative lists DUI among offenses eligible for automatic sealing and § 9122.1 has no DUI exclusion.

dismissed.note: Charges that end in dismissal, withdrawal, nolle pros or acquittal are sealed automatically within 30 days, and you can also petition the court to expunge them.
dismissed.issue: Old note omitted the automatic 30-day sealing.

domestic.note: Offenses against the family (Article D) and assault-type offenses punishable by more than 2 years cannot be sealed. A second-degree misdemeanor such as simple assault is not caught by that bar and may be sealed by petition after 7 years.
domestic.issue: App said fully barred; the exclusion applies only to Article D offenses and Article B offenses punishable by more than two years.

sexual.note: Sexual offenses and offenses requiring registration cannot be sealed, and indecent exposure within 15 years blocks sealing. A pardon is the only route.

juvenile.when: 6 months after consent decree; 2 yrs (misd.) or 5 yrs (felony) after discharge
juvenile.notes: A court orders expungement on motion: 6 months after informal adjustment or consent decree, 2 years after discharge for a misdemeanor adjudication (Act 108 of 2024) or 5 years for a felony, if no new offense. Youth 14 or older adjudicated for rape, IDSI or aggravated indecent assault are excluded.
juvenile.issue: App said 'age 18 + petition or age 21'; the age-21 provision applies to dependency records, and Act 108 of 2024 added a 2-year misdemeanor track.

RI.name: Rhode Island
RI.remedy: Expungement (sealing) of convictions; sealing of non-conviction records

misdemeanor.note: A first-time offender can petition to expunge one misdemeanor 5 years after finishing the sentence with no new arrests; people with 2 to 6 misdemeanors and no felony can apply after 10 years.
misdemeanor.issue: App said 'true' with wait from offense; relief is limited to first offenders (or up to 6 misdemeanors after 10 years) and runs from completion of sentence.

felony.note: A first-time offender can petition to expunge one non-violent felony 10 arrest-free years after finishing the sentence. Crimes of violence are never eligible.
felony.issue: App said 5 years; the felony wait is 10 years after completion of sentence.

dui.note: DUI cannot be expunged under the multiple-misdemeanor route. A first offender with a single misdemeanor DUI may qualify under the general first-offender rule after 5 years.
dui.issue: App said DUI is barred; the statutory DUI bar applies to the multiple-misdemeanor route. First-offender eligibility for DUI was not confirmed from statute text.

dismissed.note: Cases dismissed by the State on or after Jan. 1, 2023 are sealed automatically within 20 days; people acquitted or exonerated can petition for sealing. Domestic cases must wait 3 years from filing.
dismissed.issue: Old note omitted automatic sealing of dismissals (2023).

domestic.note: Domestic violence convictions cannot be expunged under the multiple-misdemeanor route, and domestic cases that were filed or dismissed wait 3 years. A first offender with one domestic misdemeanor may petition after 5 years if it is not a crime of violence.
domestic.issue: App said fully barred; the statutory DV bar applies to the multiple-misdemeanor route.

sexual.note: Serious sex offenses such as sexual assault and child molestation are crimes of violence and can never be expunged.
sexual.issue: CCRC does not separately discuss misdemeanor sex offenses; this entry rests on the crime-of-violence exclusion.

juvenile.when: At final disposition of the case
juvenile.notes: Juvenile records are sealed automatically when the case ends (dismissal, not-guilty finding or completed sentence), with limited exceptions. Felony adjudications can still be used at sentencing in adult court.
juvenile.issue: App said automatic expungement at age 18; the statute seals records at final disposition, not at a set age.

misdemeanor.note: Minor offenses punishable by no more than 30 days or a $1,000 fine can be expunged 3 years after the sentence is completed with no other conviction; this can be used only once and traffic offenses are excluded.
misdemeanor.issue: First-offender limit was repealed in 2018; wait runs from completion of sentence.

felony.note: Most felonies cannot be expunged. Exceptions: first-offense drug possession (3 years), possession with intent to distribute (20 years), Youthful Offender Act sentences (5 years after completion), and trafficking survivors.
felony.issue: App said felonies are never eligible; drug, youthful-offender and trafficking-survivor routes exist.

dui.note: DUI convictions cannot be expunged in South Carolina because traffic offenses are excluded from expungement.

dismissed.note: Dismissed, nolle prossed and acquitted charges can be expunged at no cost; in magistrate and municipal courts this happens automatically, and in General Sessions you apply through the solicitor's office.
dismissed.issue: App cited § 17-1-40; the operative statute is § 17-22-950, and summary-court expungement is automatic.

domestic.note: A first-time domestic violence 3rd-degree (or former first-offense CDV) conviction can be expunged 5 years after completing the sentence with no other conviction, once in a lifetime.
domestic.issue: App said domestic violence is barred; § 22-5-910 allows it after 5 years.

sexual.note: Sex offense convictions carry more than 30 days' imprisonment, so no South Carolina expungement statute covers them.
sexual.issue: CCRC does not separately address sex offenses; this follows from the 30-day/$1,000 limit in § 22-5-910.

juvenile.notes: At 18, a person may petition family court to expunge status or nonviolent offense adjudications if the sentence is complete and there is no later conviction or adjudication. Violent crimes and offenses carrying a 5-year adult sentence (if a prior) are excluded.
juvenile.issue: App suggested '5 years post-completion' alternative; the CCRC profile describes eligibility at age 18 with no such alternative.

SD.name: South Dakota
SD.remedy: Expungement (non-convictions); sealing after suspended imposition of sentence; automatic removal from public record for minor offenses; pardon

misdemeanor.waitFrom: conviction (5 years with no new conviction)
misdemeanor.note: Class 2 misdemeanors and petty offenses are removed from the public record automatically after 5 years if you met the court's conditions and have no new conviction. First offenders who receive a suspended imposition of sentence have the record sealed when they finish probation.
misdemeanor.issue: App cited SDCL § 23A-3-56 (not a relief statute) and a 10-year wait; the real rule is automatic removal after 5 years for Class 2 misdemeanors.

felony.note: A first offender who receives a suspended imposition of sentence is discharged without a conviction and the court must seal the record. Other felonies can be sealed only by a pardon from the Board of Pardons (generally 5 years after release for first-time felons).
felony.issue: App said felonies are not eligible; suspended imposition of sentence sealing and pardon sealing exist.

dui.note: A first DUI is a Class 1 misdemeanor, which is not covered by automatic removal. Relief is through a pardon (expedited for Class 1 misdemeanors after 10 years), which seals the record.
dui.issue: App said not eligible; the pardon route is available. Whether suspended imposition of sentence is allowed for DUI was not confirmed.

dismissed.note: You can ask the court to expunge an arrest 1 year after no charges are filed or after the case is dismissed, and at any time after an acquittal; the prosecutor may object. Completed diversion is expunged automatically.
dismissed.issue: App said 0-year wait and cited § 23A-3-56; dismissals wait 1 year under § 23A-3-27.

domestic.note: Domestic assault is usually a Class 1 misdemeanor, which is not covered by automatic removal; the main route is a pardon (expedited for Class 1 misdemeanors after 10 years). A first offender who gets a suspended imposition of sentence may have the record sealed.
domestic.issue: App said barred; pardon and suspended-imposition routes are not excluded by statute as summarized by CCRC.

sexual.note: Rape is excluded from suspended imposition of sentence, so sex offense convictions generally can be sealed only through a pardon, which is rarely granted.
sexual.issue: App said fully barred; a pardon (which seals records) remains legally available.

juvenile.when: 1 year after release from court jurisdiction, by petition
juvenile.notes: Sealing is not automatic: a person may petition 1 year after release from court jurisdiction or DOC discharge, and the court must find no later adjudications, no pending serious charges and rehabilitation. Trafficking survivors may seek vacatur and expungement.
juvenile.issue: App said 'age 18 + 1 year offense-free'; the statute measures 1 year from release from jurisdiction or discharge, with no age-18 trigger.
